issues.failure_explanation: No strict positive-definiteness or nonsingularity assumption is imposed when the inverse formula is introduced. Distinct nodes do not suffice under the paper's kernel assumptions: for example, a constant kernel satisfies the differentiability condition but has a singular Gram matrix for M>1. Thus the displayed construction and later uses of the resulting unique weight vector are undefined as stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume that the relevant Gram matrices are invertible, for example by requiring a strictly positive-definite kernel on distinct configurations, or reformulate all affected statements using possibly nonunique minimizers and a pseudoinverse.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed universal analytical formula for optimal weights, the matrix formulation of the steady-state condition, and the gradient formulas relying on those weights are unsupported for allowed singular kernels.
issues.title: Optimal-weight formula assumes an invertible kernel matrix
issues.why_classification: A standard local nonsingularity condition preserves the formulas and all principal conclusions for the intended strictly positive-definite kernels.

The Voronoi formula applies after minimizing over the weights, when the weights can be chosen as the cell masses; fixed prescribed weights generally require weighted Laguerre cells.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper imposes no assumption ensuring that every Voronoi cell has positive $\pi$-mass. For instance, with an atomic target, distinct nodes can have empty cells, making the denominator in the Lloyd map zero. Thus the map need not even be defined on all of $\mathcal X^M_{\ne}$, so the asserted closure and preservation statement does not follow.

failure_location.quote: However, $\bm{\Psi}_{\mathrm{Lloyd}}$ preserves nondegeneracy in the sense that, if $\Y \in \mathcal{X}_{\neq}^{M}$ then $\bm{\Psi}_{\mathrm{Lloyd}}(\Y) \in \mathcal{X}_{\neq}^{M}$, ensuring that the fixed-point iteration is closed

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State sufficient regularity and support assumptions guaranteeing positive cell masses and distinct updated barycenters, or explicitly restrict the claim to configurations for which these properties hold and prescribe an empty-cell rule.
issues.overall_effect: The unconditional background claim that Lloyd's fixed-point iteration is closed on all nondegenerate configurations is unreliable.
issues.title: Lloyd's map may be undefined and need not preserve nondegeneracy under the stated scope
issues.why_classification: This is a local missing-domain condition in background material and does not affect the paper's MSIP formulas.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Under the assumption that the kernel matrices $\bm{K}(\yt)$ and $\bm{\bar{K}}(\yt)$ are non-singular, the relationship \eqref{eq:msip_fixed_point_def} is expressed as a fixed-point iteration

issues.failure_explanation: Invertibility of $K(Y)$ and $\bar K(Y)$ does not imply invertibility of the diagonal matrix $W(Y)$. For example, if $\pi=\delta_{y_1}$ and $K(Y)$ is invertible, then $v_0(Y)=K(Y)e_1$ and the optimal weights are $e_1$, so all but one diagonal entries of $W$ vanish. The asserted inverse map is then undefined and the preceding linear equation does not uniquely determine the zero-weight particle positions.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require every optimal weight to be nonzero at every iterate and state the resulting restricted domain, or add a rule for deleting, retaining, or reinitializing zero-weight particles.
issues.overall_effect: The MSIP update is not defined on all configurations satisfying the paper's stated nonsingularity assumptions.
issues.title: MSIP inversion omits the required nonzero-weight condition
issues.why_classification: Adding an explicit nonzero-weight domain condition handles this degenerate case without changing the update or its advertised behavior on regular iterates.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: When $\kappa$ is the squared exponential kernel, there exists a scalar $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}$ such that $\bar{\kappa} = \lambda \kappa$; then, the condition~\eqref{eq:MMD_optimality_okq} implies $\bar{\bm{u}}(\y) = 0$

issues.failure_explanation: For M=1, the general MSIP map obtained from the paper's own formulas is $y+(\bar v_1(y)-\bar v_0(y)y)/(w\bar\kappa(y,y))$, whereas the mean-shift map is $\bar v_1(y)/\bar v_0(y)$. These maps have the same nondegenerate fixed points but are not the same iteration unless the additional identity $w\bar\kappa(y,y)=\bar v_0(y)$ holds, as it does when $\bar\kappa$ is proportional to $\kappa$. The corollary establishes coincidence of critical/fixed points, not equality of the algorithms under Assumption 2.1 alone.

failure_location.quote: Then, the mean shift algorithm becomes a special case of the fixed-point iteration defined in \Cref{sec:msip} when $M = 1$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the claim to coincidence of nondegenerate fixed points under the general assumption, and assert equality of the iterations only under an additional condition such as $\bar\kappa=\lambda\kappa$.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised interpretation of general MSIP as an extension whose one-particle case is exactly classical mean shift is overstated outside proportional-profile kernels such as the squared-exponential kernel.
issues.title: Mean shift is not the one-particle MSIP iteration for a general admissible kernel
issues.why_classification: The repair requires a substantive restriction or weakening of one of the paper's advertised conceptual connections, although the gradient and fixed-point characterizations remain comparable.
